1. RECURRENT PREGNANCY LOSS

•Work up after 2 miscarriages if abnormality is suspected
•Sggryd – 5% women
→Risk factors of Recurrent pregnancy loss:
1.Age
-Female > 35yrs
-Male > 40yrs
2.Previous miscarriages

Successful pregnancy after RPL = 60%

Further loss after RPL = 40%

3.Obesity / low BMI

<19, >25

4.Black ethnicity
5.Smoking.
6.alcohol
7.caffeine>200mg/day
→Risk factor of Sporadic miscarriages:
1.Caffeine / Tea, mostly in first trimester.
2.Alcohol.
3.Obesity.
4.Age.
5.Environmental Factors.
6.Anesthetic Gases – under Reasaerch, confliciting data.

CAUSES OF RPL AND THEIR MANAGEMENT

1.APLA:
•15% of RPL.
•2% in healthy pregnancies.
•80% success after t/m.
•10% without t/m.

Work up: offer prior to pregnancy – 2+ve test 12 weeks apart and at least 6 weeks post miscarriage.

 

-Criteria of workup>3 – 1st miscarriage before 10 weeks.
-1 – 2nd
-1 PTB before 34 weeks, due to complications like placental insufficiency early onset pre – eclampsia mainly iatrogenic birth.
1.LA:
-strongest association.
-Dilute Russel viper venom + platelet neutralization => sensitive + specific.
2.Med – high titer> 90 centile> 40IU/mlACA:
3.B2-Glycoproten:

 

Treatment: Aspirin(75mg) + LMWH(40mg) from the start of pregnancy (upt positive) till 34 weeks.

 

2.Genetics:
-2-5% of couples

balanced Translocation in 1 parent:

-Recurrent miscarriages (further miscarriages 30-57% if embryonal chromosomal abnormality).
-Anomalous babies or babies with mental disability.
-Healthy babies can also born with balanced genetic translocation.

Work-up:

-POC karyotyping of 3rd conceptus
-Parental karyotyping if

1.POC shows an un balanced translocation or

2. tissue not available for testing

Treatment: - Refer to geneticist.

•Proceed to natural pregnancy 50 – 70% healthy alive birth.
•Gamete donation + IVF.
•PGD + IVF = 30% success.
•Adoption.
3.Anatomical:
-all women with recurrent miscarriages
- 3D USG gold standard.
→Uterine anomaly1.8 – 37.6%, more in 2nd miscarriage.
•Septate – 1st and arcuate - 2ndmiscarriages.

Work up:

•USG of all women with three 1st & one 2nd miscarriage
•USG + HSG – initial screening
• 3D USG is the diagnostic test

Treatment:

Hysteroscopic septostomy – Audit /Research context.

→Cervical anomaly:
• Cause 2nd miscarriages, premature ruptured membranes or painless dilation.

Workup:

•One 2nd miscarriage or suspected Cervical weakness.
•USG measurement of Cervix.
•Serial measurements from 16 weeks to 24weeks.

Treatment:

Cervical cerclage

1.ultrasound indicated cerclage if length is ≤2.5mm

2.History indicated cerclage:

3 or more 2nd trimester miscarriages

1 or more PTB

 

Abdominal Cerclage:

•Failed Cerclage.
•Very Short or scarred Cervix.

 

4.Inherited Thrombophilia:
•Carrier of factor v, prothrombin gene mutation – double risk.

•Antithrombin 3 deficiency is rare yet most thrombogenic mutation associated with sporadic miscarriage.
•Thrombophilia testing may be offered to women with 2nd trimester miscarriage.

Work up:

-One 2nd miscarriage.
1.Factor V Leiden.
2.Factor II - prothrombin gene mutation
3.Protein S deficiency

Treatment: - 86% success in 2nd with LMWH

-29% with aspirin (Not recommended)
-Individualized Management.

5.Endocrine Factors:

•HbA1c, 1st miscarriage – workup is indicated when there is suspicion of DM but not routinely
• LH in PCOS – workup is not recommended.
•Thyroid dysfunction – workup is recommended
•Insulin in PCOS – workup is not recommended
•Hyperandrogenism – workup is not recommended
•Hyperprolactinemia has association with RPL.

6.Immunologic Factors:

•No work up or t/m recommended.

 

7.Infections:

•BV => 2nd miscarriages.
•Clindamycin treatment risk.

 

8.Thyroid Problems:

•Thyroid peroxidase antibodies r associated with RPL, so work up is offered but thyroxine is not given in euthyroid women.
•Subclinical Hypothyroidism has association with RPL.

Thyroxine supplementation:

1.Not recommended routinely with mild SCH (TSH >2.5).
2. Consider Thyroxine if TSH > 4Miu/l
3. regular TSH test from 7 – 9weeks, until 34 weeks is recommended in case of positive TPO antibodies and or/SCH because of risk of progression to overt hypothyroidism.

9.Progesterone supplementation:

•RPL + Bleeding = Micronized progesterone is recommended 400mg, Plv, twice a day from bleeding till 16weeks).

10.Unexplained RPL:

should receive only supportive care in dedicated RPL clinic.

•Supportive Therapy 75% success.
• aspirin/ heparin not recommended
• endometrial scratch test not recommended.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Tests to be carried out in all women with RPL (1st recurrent / 2nd only 1 miscarriage):

1.APLA – if +ve => LMWH + Aspirin in next pregnancy once UPT +ve.
2.Genetic tests
-Fetal.
-Parental.
3.Protein S, Factor V (2nd ) & PT gene mutation.
4.3D USG – for uterine anomalies

 

MRI and endoscopy in case of inconclusive diagnosis.

5.TPO + TSH.

 

From 7 – 9 weeks till 34 weeks.
